item-handbooktext-creature-seaserpent2: The common serpent of deep saltwater. It stalks swimmers and boats in water at least 50 blocks deep, circles for a while, then strikes at anyone in the water. It will not bite a player sitting in a boat. It retreats once you reach water less than 3 blocks deep and gives up about 30 seconds after you leave the water. When killed it sinks to the sea floor. Dive down and harvest the corpse with a knife for fish, bone, rusty gears and Jonas parts. See the Underwater Horrors guide.
item-handbooktext-creature-seaserpent: The rarer, aggressive surface serpent (about one spawn in ten). It hunts near the surface rather than in the deep and flees less readily when hurt. Same weaknesses as the sea serpent: shallow water and dry land. Its harvest includes rust loot. See the Underwater Horrors guide.
item-handbooktext-creature-giantserpent: A rust serpent grown five times over, some 220 blocks from jaw to tail, and very rare: about one serpent in fifty. It never surfaces to hiss. It circles deep below its prey, then rises mouth first out of the dark. Boats are no shelter from it: it swallows a raft in one gulp, breaks a sailboat in a few bites and leaves the crew in the water. It strikes only over deep water, so the shallows and dry land are still safe. Its carcass holds a hoard of rusty gears and Jonas parts. See the Underwater Horrors guide.
item-handbooktext-creature-krakenbody: A very rare deep water horror. The body rests on the sea floor and sends tentacles up toward a swimmer. A tentacle that reaches you grabs and drags you down; killing one of the claws around you breaks the grip. Tentacles stall and give up when you climb into a boat or onto land. See the Underwater Horrors guide.
game:uh-guide-text:
Underwater Horrors
Horrors dwell in the depths.

Lore
During the time of the Rot, many traders fled land for life on the seas. They did not live there long, however, before the corruption of the ocean became apparent. All that remains of them now are sunken shipwrecks, skeletons, and perhaps the occasional remnant of their technology from within the belly of a horror.

Where they live
Serpents and the kraken spawn only in saltwater at least 50 blocks deep, near a player who is swimming or sailing in it. Rivers, ponds and shallow coasts are safe. Only one creature is normally alive in the world at a time.

Sea Serpent
The sea serpent circles a swimmer, then strikes. It will not attack a player sitting in a boat. To escape, reach water shallower than 3 blocks or get onto land; it retreats and despawns about 30 seconds later. The rust serpent is the rarer, more aggressive surface hunter.

Rust Leviathan
Very rarely the serpent that comes is a rust leviathan, a rust serpent five times the size. It never surfaces to hiss. It circles deep below, a dark shape under the water, then rises mouth first from the dark. Boats are no shelter from it: a raft goes down in one gulp, a sailboat in a few bites, and the crew lands in the water. Make for the shallows.

Kraken
The kraken is very rare and more likely at night. Its tentacles reach up from the deep and drag a swimmer down. Kill one of the claws around you to break the grip. Tentacles cannot follow you into a boat or onto land.

Loot
A killed serpent sinks to the sea floor. Dive down and harvest it with a knife for fish, bone, rusty gears and Jonas parts, and bring breath to spare.

Ruins
Sunken ruins, wrecks and a drowned city generate on the deep sea floor. Glowing ghostlights mark them from a distance. They hold collapsed chests and piles of ingots, and most are guarded: a spawner block wakes a serpent (rarely a kraken) when you swim close. Spawner blocks cannot be mined.

Staying safe
Shallow water, land and boats, though a boat will not stop the leviathan. Creative and spectator players are ignored.

For server owners
Everything above is configurable in ModConfig/UnderwaterHorrorsConfig.json: spawn depth and chance, how many creatures may live at once, kraken chance, ruin rarity and loot, sound volumes, and freshwater spawning. The metals and sizes of ingot piles in ruins nobody has visited yet follow the current config. Admin commands live under /uh (spawn, ruins, ghostlights, observer, debug, sound) and /uhruin.
blockhelp-serpentspawner: Spawns a sea serpent when a player enters the water nearby, then vanishes until that serpent despawns.
blockhelp-krakenspawner: Spawns a kraken when a player enters the water nearby, then vanishes until that kraken despawns.
